messages:
maya: FYI running a focused triage on TritonFlare-7B (int4) warmup fragmentation. symptoms: steady traffic then sudden OOMs for long generations (>900 tokens). any recent changes to prefetch or microbatching?
zach: we flipped auto-prefetch on last week for TF models. saw an uptick in slab fragmentation metrics but assumed normal. can repro locally with a 30rps generator and mixed lengths.
linh: repro script and logs uploaded to s3://canary-artifacts/tf7b-frag/ (run-2026-03-05). core log snippet:
```
[2026-03-05T09:14:02Z] prefetch.kv: queued 3 segments
[2026-03-05T09:14:07Z] slab: free_list fragmentation 0.68
[2026-03-05T09:14:07Z] alloc failed size=96MB context=kv.fetch
[2026-03-05T09:14:07Z] OOM seq=914 max_new=1200
```
ops-bot: incident INC-9920 created and linked to canary cluster tf-canary-7b-3.
anita: quick theory: combination of large max_new + eager prefetching of KV + long-lived session caches mean the slab allocator loses large contiguous chunks. experiments to try: reduce default max_new, turn prefetch to lazy, enable slab compaction pass every 5s during low QPS, tune microbatch window to favor lower concurrency for big gens.
maya: can we run a small matrix and gather quality/latency tradeoffs? keep runs short (1h each) on 2 canaries.
linh: matrix I queued:
- E1: max_new=600, prefetch=lazy, microbatch=80ms
- E2: max_new=900, prefetch=lazy, microbatch=120ms
- E3: max_new=600, prefetch=on, slab-compact=5s
- E4: baseline (max_new=1200, prefetch=on, microbatch=40ms)

zach: early smoke (30m each) results summary:
- E1: zero OOMs, p99 latency +12%, throughput -6%
- E2: 1 soft OOM (evicted session), p99 +18%
- E3: 2 OOMs but slab fragmentation metric reduced after compaction pass
- E4: 4 OOMs, fragmentation steadily climbing

eval-bot: ran quality checks vs baseline float32 on representative prompt set:
```
E1 quality deltas: perp +0.2, qa acc -0.5% (within CI)
E2 quality deltas: perp +0.1, qa acc -0.3%
E3 quality deltas: perp +0.3, qa acc -0.7%
```

anita: interpretation: E1 is the best safety/cost compromise. moving max_new default down to 600 for int4 TF-7B eliminates OOMs with small perf hit and tiny quality delta. E3 slab compaction helped fragmentation numbers but didn't prevent OOMs fully; compaction adds jitter and overhead.
maya: propose rollout plan:
- Stage 1: push model default change (max_new=600, microbatch=80ms, prefetch=lazy) to 2 canaries for 24h.
- Stage 2: if no OOMs and p99 latency regression <25%, roll to all canaries for 48h.
- Rollback triggers: any OOM >0 or p99 regression >30% or QA drift >1.5% on eval harness.

linh: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/models/pull/482 (includes default config, smoke artifacts, slab charts and telemetry tag changes).
zach: please add telemetry tag model.tuning_reason=frag_warmup and session.metadata.prompt_len_bucket so we can slice failures.

linh: will add tags and a short Grafana dashboard panel for slab_free/alloc failures.

ops-bot: scheduled rollout job created: rollout-1810001112 (canary=2, watch=24h). linked INC-9920.
maya: thanks all. follow-up action items: linh update config PR, zach add prompt_len telemetry, anita run an extended A/B for 48h after canary green. :thumbsup:
